transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Rios (Redwood SE), Jasper Wu (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood CSM); Sara Nguyen (Atlas ML), Tom Alvarez (Atlas SRE), Priya Patel (Atlas Security), Diego Morales (Atlas Platform)

[00:00] Liam: Alright thanks everyone for joining, we were gonna walk through the Console tracing flows and how you can use request logs to debug those hallucination and latency issues you mentioned. quick intro then Maya will share screen.
[00:18] Sara: Thanks Liam. yep we've been seeing intermittent latency spikes and a few degraded outputs after model updates, trying to understand root cause and whether Redwood's tracing and request logs can help us correlate infra vs prompt issues.
[00:30] Maya: cool. i'll pull up the tracing page. bear with me, i'm on a new layout so some labels might be slightly different. you can see on the left nav there's Traces, Request Logs, and Error Analysis.
[00:50] [screen share noise] Maya: so this is the trace waterfall for a single user request. top-level timeline shows routing (hosted -> dedicated fallback), model warmup, and tokenize/generate spans. note the KV-cache miss span there, that often explains extra latency for long conversations.
[01:15] Tom: is KV cache the same as what we call the prefix cache? sometimes our app does prefix caching on the client.
[01:22] Maya: yes similar, but Redwood's KV cache is server-side per model shard, it stores past key/value attention states. if there's a miss we'll see a large decode span. sometimes caused by short LRU expiry, or different model variant being routed.
[01:40] Sara: can we filter traces by model version? we pin models in prod so want to compare v1.2 vs v1.3.
[01:47] Maya: yep, there's a model_version filter. also you can group by route, region, or Deployment Tier (Hosted/Dedicated).
[02:05] Liam: one thing customers ask is whether these traces preserve PII	1 Priya i think you had a question about redaction?
[02:15] Priya: yes, how do logs handle PHI/PII? we can't export free text offsite for many records.
[02:22] Maya: good question. Redwood Console supports on-the-fly redaction rules and also server-side encryption with customer KMS. you can configure masking for fields, and export of raw request_text can be disabled; we also have compliance mode where only metadata is stored in the Console.
[02:40] Priya: ok, can we get the SOC2 artifacts and the network diagram?
[02:45] Liam: yes we'll send the security pack after the call, SOC2 Type II, CA certs, KMS integration guidance and VPC peering diagram.
[03:00] Jasper: back to the trace. notice the orange error marker here - that's an internal model timeout. clicking it opens the Error Analysis panel with top failing prompts and embeddings mismatch heuristics.
[03:20] Sara: embeddings mismatch? our reranker has been flaky, could that show up here?
[03:26] Maya: sometimes. we surface clustering of failed responses and compare them to previous baselines, highlighting token-level deltas and prompts that produced low-quality replies. it's heuristic, not perfect, but helps prioritize.
[03:45] Tom: can we link traces to source request IDs from our app? that's important for debugging.
[03:52] Maya: yes we support correlating with your request_id	1 you can pass X-Request-ID header and it shows up in the trace metadata. we also ingest customer-side spans if you push tracing data back to Redwood via OTLP.
[04:10] Diego: what's the retention on request logs for hosted vs dedicated?
[04:15] Liam: hosted tiers default to 30d retention, enterprise and dedicated can configure longer retention and S3 export. for private/on-prem you control retention.
[04:30] Priya: how about encryption at rest and in transit?
[04:33] Maya: TLS in transit always. at rest we use AES-256 and can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key control.
[04:40] Sara: can we demo request logs export?
[04:42] Maya: yep i'll jump to Request Logs. here you can filter by time range, tokens_consumed, latency, status codes, and custom metadata. export button allows CSV/JSON or direct S3 delivery.
[05:05] [Maya clicks] Maya: i'm triggering an export of a one-hour window. you'll see exported file schema contains request_id, user_id (if you send), model_version, tokens_in/tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code, and optional masked request_text.
[05:25] Tom: if we do S3 export, can we set up a lifecycle to purge sensitive data?
[05:29] Maya: yes you control lifecycle on the S3 bucket; Redwood can write to your bucket with a restricted IAM role.
[05:40] Sara: what about alerting	1 we want to be notified when hallucination rates spike or latency SLOs breach.
[05:47] Maya: Error Analysis has metric-based alerts and anomaly detection. you can create alerts on error_rate, avg_latency_p95, and set a baseline from historical data. alerts can be sent to PagerDuty, Slack, or email.
[06:05] Liam: quick aside	1 routing policies: if Dedicated capacity is overloaded we can fallback to a compatible hosted variant; traces will show that routing decision for each request.
[06:20] Diego: that fallback behavior worries us; if a request silently goes to hosted, data residency may be violated. can we disable auto-fallback?
[06:28] Maya: yes, for enterprise you can disable fallback and queue/return 429s instead. you'll see explicit trace annotations for fallback events when enabled.
[06:45] Sara: ok can you show an example of a hallucination-related trace?
[06:50] Maya: sure	1 here's a trace where the model returned a factual error. the Error Analysis clusters similar failures and surfaces the top contributing prompts. note the confidence heuristic and token-level surprise score.
[07:10] Tom: how reliable is the 'surprise score'? we've seen false positives.
[07:15] Maya: it's statistical; we recommend pairing with a small eval set and running Redwood Optimize to recommend model/quantization changes. it flags candidates, not final verdicts.
[07:33] [10 min mark - skipping ahead in transcript to mid-call debugging demo]
[10:05] Maya: i'm switching to live request replay	1 we can replay a historical request against a pinned model in a sandboxed environment. this helps reproduce regressions after model upgrades.
[10:25] Sara: nice, can we re-run with our prompt tweaks?
[10:28] Maya: yep you can edit the prompt inline and replay; results are stored under the replay run with diffs.
[10:38] Tom: any risk that replays expose PII?
[10:41] Maya: if replays contain raw text, they obey your redaction and retention policies; you can choose to mask before replay.
[11:00] [15 min mark - performance profiling deep dive]
[15:05] Jasper: here's a request that spiked to 1.2s	1 tracing shows a model compilation cache miss on the GPU host, related to a new quantization kernel. we flagged it in the kernel selection logs.
[15:22] Diego: kernel selection logs? can we pull those across?
[15:25] Jasper: yes for Dedicated you can enable debug kernel logs; for hosted we surface aggregated kernel metrics in the Console.
[15:35] Tom: are quantization changes surfaced as part of model_version metadata?
[15:39] Maya: yes model metadata includes quantization profile, sequence length distribution, and recommended batch sizes.
[15:45] Sara: how do we run load tests? we need predictable throughput numbers to size Dedicated.
[15:50] Liam: we offer a benchmarking harness; Redwood SEs can run a simulated workload with your prompts to estimate throughput and cost. that's part of the POC.
[16:05] Maya: i'm going to show the Error Analysis dashboard. we surface top failing prompts, rate of regression compared to baseline, and a per-route token cost breakdown.
[16:25] Priya: does Error Analysis store the full request_text or only embeddings / hashes?
[16:30] Maya: configurable	1 by default we store masked text and full logs if you opt-in. for stricter compliance we store only metadata and embeddings.
[16:45] Sara: ok, can we set up a canary rollout with alerts on quality regressions?
[16:52] Maya: yes	1 rollouts support canary percentages, automatic quality checks using your eval set, and automatic rollback if regression threshold exceeded. the Console shows the rollout timeline and traces for canary requests.
[17:10] Tom: question about cost attribution	1 can we see token-level cost per route?
[17:14] Liam: yes the cost breakdown shows tokens_in/out, compute tier, and estimated $ cost per request; for Dedicated you get a normalized unit cost for capacity utilization.
[17:30] Diego: for the POC, we'd like Redwood to run traces against our staging with 2k requests/hour. is that feasible?
[17:36] Maya: feasible	1 we normally recommend a week-long run to gather meaningful baselines. we'll need an IAM role for S3 export and a staging API key with limited scope.
[17:52] Sara: one more security question	1 SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning?
[17:56] Olivia: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for user management, and RBAC with fine-grained roles including auditor-only view.
[18:10] Priya: do you log admin actions on the Console? we need audit trails.
[18:14] Olivia: yes audit logs are available and can be pushed to your SIEM. they include user actions, config changes, and export events.
[18:28] [20 min mark - closing in on next steps]
[20:30] Liam: recap	1 we'll send SOC2 and security pack, Maya will share the runbook and the sample queries to use for the tracing POC, and we'll schedule the POC for week of Dec 13. Sara will provide sample failing request IDs and test prompts.
[20:48] Sara: sounds good. one ask	1 can you include a cost estimate for Dedicated vs hosted for our 2k rps simulated workload?
[20:56] Liam: yes we'll include that in the pricing doc.
[21:05] Tom: also include the S3 export flow diagram and IAM role template.
[21:10] Liam: will do.
[21:20] [brief crosstalk, some people dropping to handle PagerDuty alerts]
[22:00] Maya: small demo note	1 when you click into a failed cluster we display representative requests and a small diff view. sometimes transcription shows slightly wrong model names, that's because of OCR on auto-captured images, ignore that.
[22:25] Sara: ha yeah we've seen that in other tools.
[22:35] [wrap up] Liam: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the pilot contract. any final q's?
[22:44] Priya: none from security, thank you.
[22:47] Diego: thumbs up.
[22:49] Sara: thanks all.
[22:52] Liam: bye.

Notes about transcript quality: some entity names and kernel labels transcribed imperfectly (e.g., 'KV cache' -> 'K V cash' in one span). There was occasional crosstalk and short dropouts around 21:20 due to participant PagerDuty interruptions.
